draft.title: Structure across a whole text
card: Structure is how a whole text is ordered. Writers arrange it in parts such as chapters, acts, scenes or stanzas.
The order is a choice. A writer decides what comes first, what is held back and what comes last.
Order can build tension, for example by delaying an answer. It can set up contrast, for example by placing a calm scene next to a violent one.
Order can also shape the final effect. A text that ends where it began may suggest nothing has changed. A sudden ending may leave the reader unsettled.
draft.remember: Structure is the order of the whole text, and that order is chosen to create an effect.

a.q: What does structure mean when studying a whole text?
opts: How the text is ordered as a whole
The time and place the text was written
An image that returns through the text
The type of story with expected features
a.why: Structure is about the order of parts such as chapters, acts or stanzas. The option about time and place describes context, which is a different idea.
a.clue: Think about how the parts are arranged from start to finish.

b.q: In a novel, the narrator hints on page one that something terrible happened but explains it only in the last chapter. What effect does this ordering mainly create?
opts: Tension, because the reader waits for the answer
Contrast, because two scenes sit side by side
A final effect of repeating the opening scene
A sense that the writer has ignored the order
b.why: Holding back the explanation until the end keeps the reader curious, which builds tension. Contrast needs two different parts placed together, and the example describes no such pairing.
b.clue: Ask what the reader feels while waiting for the explanation.

a.best: How the text is ordered as a whole

b.best: Tension, because the reader waits for the answer

problems.detail: The clue 'Ask what the reader feels while waiting for the explanation' echoes the right option's wording ('the reader waits for the answer'). This points students to the answer without them applying the idea.
